verdict_rationale: A deterministic, well-specified metric with trivial-baseline floor, a non-binding ceiling, a near-identical public/held-out distribution and a high-fidelity self-check; the issues are rules that are promised or implied but not enforced (training-data provenance, use of the public validation images, the shared submission volume between the encode and decode phases), none of which changes a winner.
floor: 0 = empty text (task.yaml:52-54). Sensible: a blind decoder that emits fluent unrelated text gets about 0.04 raw (~4.5 points) per ocr_text.py:20-22, and the near-blind DeepSeek/Muse trials sit at 0.017-0.039 raw (1.9-4.4 points), so the bottom few points are 'content-free text', not reading.
ceiling: 100 = unmodified DeepSeek-OCR Base mode (256 vision tokens, far over the 2 KB budget) reading the full image, 0.8931 on the 400 held-out pages; 0.8978 on the 100 public pages (task.yaml:52-56). Not binding: best trial 0.7375 raw = 82.6. It is an uncapped-information reference, so 100 is a sensible 'as good as reading the pixels' anchor; clamped above.
usable_range: observed 0-82.6 of 0-100 across 57 trials (16 of 19 nonzero at each wallet; max 56.1/67.9/82.6 at $10/$50/$200). Almost the whole range is usable.
feasible_at_10: yes: Fable 56.1 and Sonnet 55.8 at $10 (~2.9 H100-SXM hours); a frozen DeepEncoder + PCA/FSQ bottleneck + frozen/fine-tuned DeepSeek decoder is cheap to train.
budget_scaling: Plausible and observed for strong agents: Opus 26.9 -> 54.4 -> 82.6, Astra 36.4 -> 57.5 -> 64.1, Fable 56.1 -> 67.9 -> 67.8. Inverted for Argon/Muse because their architectures changed between wallets. All-model wallet means 19.9 / 23.1 / 22.8.
selfcheck_fidelity: High. verifier.py:101-175 runs grading's two isolated phases on fresh instances with full-size batches (400 encodes, ~420 decodes) at the graded 1 image/s deadline, the codebook_size cross-check and the parsers. Gaps: no architecture review (a failed review zeros the run: 2 such zeros in 57 trials), public images are repeated (~4x) so a caching server measures faster (noted to the agent, verifier.py:116-120), and the bit budget is smoke-checked on one image only (the batch does count over-budget images).
judge: none for the metric (deterministic word-level Levenshtein, ocr_text.py). The pass/fail architecture review is Claude Opus 5.5 (global).
neutrality: No judge, no vendor-specific format. DeepSeek-OCR is supplied and defines the ceiling; every scored trial used it, so it is a shared starting point, not an advantage to any agent family (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash scored lowest). Held-out text is fresh arXiv text rendered by a private HTML generator; a public agent-side renderer is not supplied, so each agent builds its own training renderer - equal for all harnesses.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared interface smoke fixture (identical md5 across tasks): /encode returns [] with codebook_size 2 and /decode returns "" (solution/server.py:87-90), which scores 0 and fails the review (no architecture.json). The organizer's compliant PCA baseline (tests/task/baselines/make_pca_submission.py, measure_baselines.py) and FSQ pilot (baselines/fsq_pilot.py:1, 'kill criterion >= 0.2 on the sparsest bucket') show solvability, but their scores are not recorded in the repo. The trials themselves show the task is solvable up to 0.74 raw.

issues.finding: The contract promises a training-data provenance check, but the task's review policy has no such check, so the stated data rule ('do not train, fine-tune, calibrate or select on the validation or test split of any public dataset') is not enforced by anything.
evidence: tasks/maple-vlm/tests/task/review.py:17 and tasks/music-transcription/tests/task/review.py:23 do have a training-provenance check
issues.affects: All wallets; favours an agent willing to select or train on forbidden data (no trial found doing so on a public benchmark split).

issues.finding: Whether the shipped public images may be used for checkpoint selection is ambiguous: they are called 'validation' and the rule forbids selecting on 'the validation ... split of any public dataset', while maple-vlm and music-transcription explicitly free their shipped examples and this task does not. Agents split: Fable 12nqia selected checkpoints on them; DeepSeek, Argon and Astra treated it as forbidden.
evidence: tasks/ocr-latent-compression/instruction.md:9 'Do not train, fine-tune, calibrate or select on the validation or test split of any public dataset'
issues.affects: Small upside for agents that read the rule loosely; effect looked negligible (Fable 0.610 public vs 0.6055 held-out).

issues.finding: The encode/decode isolation relies on the LLM review, not on the sandbox: both grading phases extract the submission from the same per-trial volume and the verifier does not check which sandbox a phase ran in, while serve.sh may write to /submission. A side channel (encoder writing text the decoder reads) is caught only if the reviewer spots it.
evidence: tasks/ocr-latent-compression/tests/task/verifier.py:6-9 'Both instances extract the submission from the same per-trial submission volume ... nothing here checks which sandbox a phase ran in ... relies on ... the review policy'
tasks/ocr-latent-compression/environment/validation/CONTRACT.md:24-25 'serve.sh runs as an unprivileged user that can write to /submission'
issues.affects: Gameability risk only; whether the volume is writable from the GPU sandbox was not established (suspected low). No trial attempted it.

issues.finding: Held-out page text is drawn from recent arXiv (titles, abstracts and CC-BY full text), and 'other public corpora are fine'; an agent that rendered training pages from a current arXiv snapshot could train its decoder's language prior on the exact held-out text. The source window is only given as an example in the builder, not recorded here. Opus 2pu2n0 used librarian-bots/arxiv-metadata-snapshot shard 00000 (likely old IDs), so no overlap is shown.
evidence: tasks/ocr-latent-compression/tests/task/ocr_latent_sources.py:3-11 'Two kinds of text, both created after every relevant model cutoff: arXiv metadata ... --from 2026-09-01 --until 2026-09-21'
tasks/ocr-latent-compression/instruction.md:9 'training splits and other public corpora are fine'
issues.affects: Would favour agents that happen to pull recent arXiv text; not observed.

issues.finding: Throughput is all-or-nothing per phase: 400 encodes in 400 s and ~420 decodes in ~420 s from readiness at concurrency 16; a miss raises 'Batch exceeded ... score is zero'. The self-check reproduces this exactly on the grading hardware, and no trial was zeroed by it.
evidence: tasks/ocr-latent-compression/tests/task/verifier.py:104-105 '400 and 420 requests at 1 image/s are 400 s and 420 s deadlines'

issues.finding: Malformed (wrong-shape) /encode and /decode responses score 0 for the image but are not counted toward the 1-in-20 run-failure limit (only transport failures are), which is more lenient than CONTRACT.md says and than the other tasks' shared evaluator.
evidence: tasks/ocr-latent-compression/environment/validation/validate.py:104-110 'failures.record(...) return None' only for RequestFailure; parse errors 'return None'
tasks/ocr-latent-compression/environment/validation/CONTRACT.md:33-35 'or answers in an undocumented shape ... Up to one evaluation request in twenty may fail that way'
issues.affects: Slightly lenient to broken servers; no trial affected.
